status_as_of_cutoff: local process as of 2026-08-11: Williams County minutes confirm the Board of County Commissioners approved Teton Digital's appeal for the data center facility, excluding battery storage, on 2025-02-18 by 4-0 recorded vote. County packet materials describe Trinity 1 as a 100 MW+ liquid-cooled data center in Dry Fork, with 30 MW Phase 1 targeted for Q3/Q4 2025 and Phase 2 tied to a new company-built substation. Teton Digital's current website claims Phase II Conditional Use Permit secured for 70 MW and Phase I in final permitting for 30 MW, but no later official county CUP, building permit, construction, inspection, CO, utility interconnection, energization, commissioning, or live-service record was located in this refresh.
evidence_grade: B - official Williams County minutes and packet documents verify appeal approval and planned project attributes; later Phase II CUP/Phase I final-permitting status is owner-reported and was not independently matched to a public county permit record.

actions.result_status: Development Services determined a CUP for the proposed data center could not be applied for because the proposed location did not meet the one-mile setback from sensitive properties and could also fail the three-mile data-center separation requirement if the nearby crypto-currency mining data center were approved.

actions.access_caveat: Official county PDF; describes pre-application intake denial, not final project denial.
actions.evidence_note: Establishes that the project entered county process and was initially blocked by setback requirements before appeal.
